context: Build one shared boundary contract and drive it through the public payload, private/export metadata, and database serialization paths. Test raw_config, raw_metadata, and each normalized mapping with distinct sentinels, plus non-secret tuning fields that must survive. Re-drive the exact unfixed gate immediately before implementation because #1468 is currently open and conflicting. Do not treat a passing focused test on one mapping as coverage of the other layers. The corrected gate uses build_result_payload default sanitization; it must not disable the very boundary under test.
description: Close the remaining platform metadata egress gap across public result payloads, private exports, and ResultDatabase metadata. The landed raw_config work covers one source, but current develop and the candidate boundary still allow raw_metadata plus normalized platform_deployment, platform_cloud, platform_compute, and platform_storage mappings to carry credential-shaped values. Include raw_config in the same boundary contract so the successor is complete even if the open #1468 branch merges first. Preserve legitimate benchmark tuning/configuration fields and apply filtering structurally at the export chokepoints rather than by a deny-list of only the observed keys. This successor repairs the create-time scope omission found by adversarial lint: database.py and schema.py test coverage is explicitly included. This is the corrected successor of credential-egress-platform-metadata-boundary-v2; its stored rung was repaired during adversarial plan review.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not duplicate the open #1468 implementation without re-driving its raw_metadata and normalized-block gaps.
anti_patterns.instead: Treat #1468 as a dependency and make this successor’s gate cover all sources and layers.
anti_patterns.why: That branch’s direct probe still leaks normalized mapping sentinels and raw_metadata.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not redact all platform metadata indiscriminately.
anti_patterns.instead: Filter credential-shaped material structurally and assert preservation of representative non-secret fields.
anti_patterns.why: Downstream benchmark analysis depends on legitimate tuning/configuration values.

anti_patterns.dont: Do not sanitize only raw_config or only the public payload.
anti_patterns.instead: Drive distinct sentinels through every export and database chokepoint.
anti_patterns.why: The defect is a multi-boundary value-materialisation gap and the private/database layers are separate consumers.

preserves.behavior: All public, private, and database serialization entry points.
Existing anonymize=False private/export semantics except for credential material that must never egress.
Non-secret benchmark tuning and platform metadata needed by downstream analysis.
